use: For plans, dates and orders once they're settled; who decided stays unsaid.

example.ja: 何食べるか決まった？
example.english: Have you decided what to eat?

examplePolite.romaji: nani o taberu ka kimarimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 何を食べるか決まりましたか？
examplePolite.english: Have you decided what you'll have?

notes: Kimeru is the 'I decide it' partner. Waiters ask 'gochuumon wa okimari desu ka?' (ready to order?).

use: For food, money, time or people still there after the rest has gone.

example.ja: ケーキ、まだ残ってる？
example.english: Is there any cake left?

examplePolite.romaji: keeki wa mada nokotte imasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: ケーキはまだ残っていますか？
examplePolite.english: Is there any cake left?

notes: Nokosu is 'leave it' (you do it). Kaisha ni nokoru = stay late at the office.

use: Things going on by themselves: rain, a streak, a story; on screen it means 'to be continued'.

example.romaji: kono ame, itsu made tsuzuku n darou.
example.ja: この雨、いつまで続くんだろう。
example.english: I wonder how long this rain will keep up.

examplePolite.romaji: kono ame wa itsu made tsuzuku n deshou ne.
examplePolite.ja: この雨はいつまで続くんでしょうね。
examplePolite.english: I wonder how long this rain will keep up.

notes: Tsuzukeru is 'keep doing it' (you continue something): benkyou o tsuzukeru.

use: Lights, fires and screens going off by themselves; also people or things vanishing.

example.ja: 急に電気が消えた。
example.english: The lights suddenly went out.

examplePolite.romaji: kyuu ni denki ga kiemashita.
examplePolite.ja: 急に電気が消えました。
examplePolite.english: The lights suddenly went out.

notes: Kesu is 'turn off, erase' (you do it): denki o kesu.

use: The door or shop opens by itself or is open; for 'I open it' use akeru.

example.ja: あの店、何時に開く？
example.english: What time does that shop open?

examplePolite.romaji: ano mise wa nanji ni akimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: あの店は何時に開きますか？
examplePolite.english: What time does that shop open?

notes: Same sound as aku 空く, be free: kono seki aite imasu ka? (is this seat free?). Read hiraku, the same kanji means open a book or hold an event.

english: increase; go up; grow in number
use: Numbers, weight, people or work going up by themselves.

example.ja: 最近体重が増えた。
example.english: I've put on weight lately.

examplePolite.romaji: saikin taijuu ga fuemashita.
examplePolite.ja: 最近体重が増えました。
examplePolite.english: I've put on weight lately.

notes: Fuyasu is 'increase it' (you do it). Opposite: heru, go down.

use: Takes ni (shigoto ni nareru); mostly heard as nareta (got used to it) or narete iru (am used to it).

example.ja: 新しい仕事、もう慣れた？
example.english: Used to the new job yet?

examplePolite.romaji: atarashii shigoto ni wa mou naremashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 新しい仕事にはもう慣れましたか？
examplePolite.english: Have you got used to the new job yet?

notes: Same sound as nareru, 'can become' (the potential of naru).

english: come out (teeth, hair); slip out, leave (a meeting, group); go through
use: Something coming loose or out, or a person leaving partway: a meeting, a club, a job.

example.ja: ごめん、ちょっと抜けるね。
example.english: Sorry, I'm going to slip out for a bit.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, chotto nukemasu.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、ちょっと抜けます。
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, I'll step out for a moment.

notes: Nuku is 'pull out, skip' (you do it): asagohan o nuku = skip breakfast.

use: Machines and objects breaking down by themselves.

example.ja: エアコン壊れちゃった。
example.english: The AC's broken.

examplePolite.romaji: eakon ga kowarete shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: エアコンが壊れてしまいました。
examplePolite.english: The air conditioner has broken.

notes: Kowasu is 'break it' (you do it). For glass or a cracked screen, wareru is the word.

use: Water, tears and time flowing; music playing in a shop; plans that get called off.

example.ja: 店でこの曲流れてた。
example.english: This song was playing in the shop.

examplePolite.romaji: mise de kono kyoku ga nagarete imashita.
examplePolite.ja: 店でこの曲が流れていました。
examplePolite.english: This song was playing in the shop.

notes: Nagasu is 'let flow' (you do it): toire o nagasu = flush the toilet.

english: pile up; build up; be saved up
use: Things building up you don't want (stress, dishes, work) or do want (money, points).

example.ja: 最近ストレスたまってる。
example.english: I've been so stressed lately.

examplePolite.romaji: saikin sutoresu ga tamatte imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 最近ストレスがたまっています。
examplePolite.english: I've been under a lot of stress lately.

notes: Tameru is 'save up, let pile up' (you do it): okane o tameru.

use: You make something go up: hours, staff, savings, friends.

example.ja: 来月からバイト増やす。
example.english: I'm taking more part-time shifts from next month.

examplePolite.romaji: raigetsu kara baito o fuyashimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 来月からバイトを増やします。
examplePolite.english: I'm taking on more part-time shifts from next month.

notes: Fueru is 'it increases' (by itself). Opposite: herasu, cut down.

use: Sounds official; casually it's mostly the cry 'kettei!' (that's settled) or 'X ni kettei' (we'll go with X).

example.ja: じゃあ、ラーメンに決定！
example.english: Right, ramen it is!

examplePolite.romaji: jaa, raamen ni kettei desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: じゃあ、ラーメンに決定ですね。
examplePolite.english: Right, so ramen it is.

notes: Kettei suru is formal; in conversation say kimeru (decide) or kimaru (be decided).

use: Upbeat word for events, races, projects and new chapters; also the noun 'a start' (ii sutaato).

example.romaji: juuji ni sutaato suru kara, okurenai de ne.
example.ja: 10時にスタートするから、遅れないでね。
example.english: It starts at ten, so don't be late.

examplePolite.romaji: juuji ni sutaato shimasu node, okurenai de kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 10時にスタートしますので、遅れないでください。
examplePolite.english: It starts at ten, so please don't be late.

notes: Hajimaru (it starts) and hajimeru (start it) are the everyday native verbs.

use: Changing something already set; a little formal, common with staff and at work.

example.ja: 予約の時間、変更できる？
example.english: Can I change the booking time?

examplePolite.romaji: yoyaku no jikan o henkou dekimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 予約の時間を変更できますか？
examplePolite.english: Could I change the time of my booking?

notes: Casually, kaeru also works: yotei o kaeru. Henka is change that happens; henkou is change you make.

use: Things catching or being on fire; also feeling fired up.

example.romaji: moeru gomi wa getsuyoubi da yo.
example.ja: 燃えるゴミは月曜日だよ。
example.english: Burnable trash goes out on Mondays.

examplePolite.romaji: moeru gomi wa getsuyoubi desu.
examplePolite.ja: 燃えるゴミは月曜日です。
examplePolite.english: Burnable trash goes out on Mondays.

notes: Moyasu is 'burn it' (you do it). Moenai gomi = non-burnable trash.

english: be all there; be complete; match
use: Mostly for people or things all being present: zen'in sorotta (everyone's here).

example.ja: 全員そろった？じゃあ、始めよう。
example.english: Everyone here? Okay, let's start.

examplePolite.romaji: zen'in soroimashita ka? dewa, hajimemashou.
examplePolite.ja: 全員そろいましたか？では、始めましょう。
examplePolite.english: Is everyone here? Then let's begin.

notes: Soroeru is 'get together, make match' (you do it): saizu o soroeru.

use: Casual; posting photos or videos online, or pay, prices or level going up.

example.romaji: kinou no shashin, insuta ni appu shita yo.
example.ja: 昨日の写真、インスタにアップしたよ。
example.english: I posted yesterday's photos on Insta.

examplePolite.romaji: kinou no shashin o insuta ni appu shimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 昨日の写真をインスタにアップしました。
examplePolite.english: I posted yesterday's photos on Instagram.

notes: As a suffix it means a rise: kyuuryou appu (pay rise), reberu appu. Opposite: daun.

english: grow (hair, nails); stretch; improve; go soggy (noodles)
use: Things getting longer by themselves; also skills or sales growing.

example.ja: 髪、伸びたね。
example.english: Your hair's grown.

examplePolite.romaji: kami ga nobimashita ne.
examplePolite.ja: 髪が伸びましたね。
examplePolite.english: Your hair has grown.

notes: Nobasu is 'grow it, stretch it' (you do it). Raamen ga nobiru = the ramen goes soggy.

english: cut down on; hold back from; refrain
use: Cutting back on food, drink or habits; notices use it for a polite 'please don't'.

example.ja: 最近お酒控えてるんだ。
example.english: I'm cutting back on drinking these days.

examplePolite.romaji: saikin osake o hikaete imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 最近お酒を控えています。
examplePolite.english: I'm cutting back on alcohol these days.

notes: Signs say 'ohikae kudasai', please refrain.
